title: Microsoft Open-Sources TauGrid to Simplify AI Workload Management on Kubernetes
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/microsoft-taugrid-open-source/en/headerimage/microsoft-phi-4-1789581142435.jpeg"/><p>Microsoft has open-sourced TauGrid, a cloud-native platform designed to manage, schedule, and monitor AI workloads on GPU-enabled Kubernetes clusters.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Lyft Moves Streaming Fleet to Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/lyft-flink-k8s-operator/en/headerimage/header-1788786681315.jpeg"/><p>Lyft has moved hundreds of production Flink jobs from a 2020 in-house Kubernetes operator to the Apache Flink Kubernetes Operator, unlocking last-state upgrades, in-place autoscaling and resource autotuning across the fleet.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Dropbox Outlines How Focusing on Existing Infrastructure Efficiency Can Create Headroom for AI
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/dropbox-datacenter/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789513176018.jpg"/><p>Dropbox has outlined how a decade of infrastructure optimization is helping it absorb growing demand from AI without treating new data-center capacity as the only answer. Its work spans forecasting, fleet utilization, storage density, hardware lifecycles, and rack-level power delivery, much of it predating the current AI boom.</p> <i>By Matt Foster</i>

title: AI-Assisted Discovery Helps Microsoft Patch More Than 1,000 Vulnerabilities in a Month
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/microsoft-ai-security-patch/en/headerimage/microsoft-llm-contextual-privacy-1789488709548.jpeg"/><p>With its latest September 2026 Patch, which addresses more than 950 vulnerabilities, Microsoft has patched about 2,750 vulnerabilities so far this year. While many attribute this surge to AI-assisted security research, organizations may struggle to keep pace and fully benefit from these advances, particularly when it comes to evaluating, prioritizing, and deploying patches.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Atlassian Automates Root Cause Analysis by Correlating Metrics, Logs and Traces
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/atlassian-automated-rca/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789026479583.jpg"/><p>Atlassian has outlined a new approach to automating root cause analysis for large-scale cloud-native incidents, using correlation across metrics, logs, distributed traces, and service topology to generate ranked hypotheses about where failures originate and how they propagate.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Amazon Linux 2027 Enters Public Preview with SELinux Enforcing by Default
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/amazon-linux-2027-preview/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789307005573.jpg"/><p>AWS has released Amazon Linux 2027 in public preview, built on the AL2023 baseline with kernel 7.1 and SELinux in enforcing mode by default. Applications that pass on AL2023's permissive mode may fail under enforcing. The announcement gives no AL2023 end-of-support date, no GA date, and no in-place migration path.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Agoda Replaces 72-Shard SQL Server Price Cache with DragonflyDB
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/agoda-price-cache-dragonflydb/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787939534250.jpg"/><p>Agoda migrated its 1.5 TB hotel Price Cache from 72 SQL Server shards to DragonflyDB to handle growing read and write volumes. The migration used staged dual reads, parity validation, gradual traffic shifting, and decentralized failover detection. Agoda reports an approximately eightfold reduction in P99 read latency, with two DragonflyDB clusters providing high availability.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Lambda SnapStart Comes to Container Images, Ending a Packaging Tradeoff
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/lambda-snapstart-container-image/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789052932475.jpg"/><p>AWS has extended Lambda SnapStart to container image functions, which hold up to 10 GB against 250 MB for zip archives. Teams previously chose between dependency headroom and sub-second startup. A Reddit thread from a month earlier shows what that cost: stripping whitespace and docstrings from installed packages to stay under the limit.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Netflix Reworks Conductor for 420 Million Monthly Workflow Executions and 10X Larger Workflows
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/netflix-conductor-4-workflow/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1787938102526.jpg"/><p>Netflix has reworked its Conductor workflow orchestration engine to handle larger workloads, increasing supported workflow size from about 2,500 to 30,000 tasks and reducing p99 workflow evaluation latency by about 40%. Conductor 4.0 separates workflow metadata from task data, moves evaluation to asynchronous processing, and introduces dynamic worker allocation and concurrency controls.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Terraform AWS Provider Continues Rapid Expansion as AWS Infrastructure Becomes More Complex
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/terraform-aws-provider-6-62/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788446872951.jpg"/><p>The Terraform AWS Provider continues its rapid evolution, with v6.62.0 adding support for new AWS capabilities while improving how Terraform understands and manages existing infrastructure.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Presentation: How to Run on Three Clouds at Once, and When Not to
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/form3-multicloud-architecture/en/mediumimage/ross-mcfarlane-kevin-holditch-medium-1788338652847.jpg"/><p>Ross McFarlane and Kevin Holditch discuss Form3's evolution from a single-cloud setup to a triple active multi-cloud architecture. They share key engineering strategies for cross-cloud networking, distributed databases with CockroachDB and NATS, custom Kubernetes operators, and navigating distinct regional disaster recovery expectations across the UK, Europe, and US financial markets.</p> <i>By Ross McFarlane, Kevin Holditch</i>

title: Session Traces and Cost Controls Help Diagnose AI Agent Failures
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/observability-ai-agents/en/headerimage/header-1788722438219.jpeg"/><p>Session traces and cost controls are emerging as key observability techniques for diagnosing AI agent failures, helping teams spot tool-call loops and runaway spend while preserving enough execution context for post-incident debugging.</p> <i>By Mark Silvester</i>

title: Presentation: Fixing the AI Infra Scale Problem by Stuffing 1M Sandboxes in a Single Server
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/unikraft-microvm-sandboxes-cloud-scaling/en/mediumimage/felipe-huici-medium-1787813506607.jpg"/><p>Felipe Huici explains how Unikraft achieves millisecond cold boots, stateful scale-to-zero, and extreme density for sandboxing AI workloads. He discusses isolation primitives, Linux kernel optimizations, and snapshotting tricks, demonstrating how to maintain sub-10ms performance at scale while integrating seamlessly into Kubernetes environments with hardware-level security.</p> <i>By Felipe Huici</i>

title: Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid Reaches GA with Licensing Details Unpublished
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/avd-hybrid-ga/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788339494959.jpg"/><p>Microsoft has made Azure Virtual Desktop Hybrid generally available. Session hosts run on customer hardware through Azure Arc while brokering stays in Azure. The Hybrid service license is unpriced, Windows Server support requires RDS CALs with Software Assurance, and multi-session Windows is not supported at all.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: HashiCorp Packer 1.16 Adds Native SLSA Provenance Generation and Verification for Machine Images
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/hashicorp-packer-verification/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788853414930.jpg"/><p>HashiCorp has released Packer v1.16.0, adding native support for generating, signing, and verifying SLSA provenance attestations for every image the tool builds. The release provides teams with a secure, tamper-proof record of how a machine image was made. It does this without needing extra supply-chain tools.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>
